A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sharpness–representation compression study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v4 reports original training trajectories, correlation analyses, evaluations of 181 pretrained ViT models, and held-out test analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports test-accuracy trajectories for the learning-rate and batch-size studies.

M1.justification: The network architectures, training objectives, and numerical MLS/adaptive-sharpness estimation procedures are retained. The new internal-feature bounds extend the theoretical analysis rather than introduce an algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: The CIFAR-10, FashionMNIST, pretrained-ViT, and all-versus-misclassified test-sample studies remain. Language modeling, retrieval, and face recognition appear as possible applications of the new theory, without corresponding experiments.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison measures remain unchanged, including Petzka et al.'s relative flatness in the pairwise analyses. Newly cited SAM and label-noise SGD work supplies context, not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Four trajectory figures replace training loss with test accuracy: v4 Figures 1, 2, H.9, and H.10 become v5 Figures 2, 3, I.10, and I.11. The stated learning rates, batch sizes, sample counts, and model configurations remain unchanged; rerunning the experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The existing learning-rate and batch-size sensitivity studies gain test-accuracy comparisons, checking whether lower sharpness accompanies better generalization. The bound-tightness, correlation, dimensionality, and misclassified-sample analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains averaging over five random initializations, and the correlation studies retain Pearson coefficients. No new uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Test-accuracy trajectories replace four training-loss series and support the added observation that lower sharpness need not imply better accuracy. Existing correlation values remain unchanged, including the MLP MLS–bound correlation of -0.60 in v4 Figure G.7 and v5 Figure H.8.

T1.justification: New Section 3.5 and Appendix A derive bounds for penultimate and intermediate features involving minimum singular values, substantially extending the formal scope. v5 also revises LVR from det(J^T J) to det(J J^T) for the rectangular Jacobian and corrects the weighted adaptive-sharpness error expression. However, new Equation (23) states equality where the derivation supports an inequality.

C1.justification: The central sharpness–compression claims remain. The introduction adds a fifth contribution connecting the framework to internal representations and neural collapse, extending the contribution list without replacing the principal LVR/MLS findings.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands qualifications concerning weight-dependent prefactors, the absence of guaranteed compression, and MSE versus cross-entropy sharpness. It also distinguishes local robustness from global neural collapse and develops the distinction between noise robustness and sensitivity to meaningful input differences in explaining generalization.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix J promises code release after acceptance; v5's abstract and Appendix K state availability and provide a repository URL. The GPU description and numerical approximation instructions remain unchanged. Actual repository accessibility was not checked.

R1.justification: v5 adds focused literature connections supporting Hessian-trace minimization and neural collapse, including Bartlett et al. (2023), Damian et al. (2021), and Jiang et al. (2023). The central positioning as an extension of Ma and Ying remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical explanations, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Terminology, assumptions, and bound-tightness discussions receive explicit signposting, while the existing reparametrization appendix is reorganized into named definitions and propositions.

P2.justification: v5 adopts a different journal layout and title-page format, adds the flatness–generalization schematic in Figure 1, and rearranges v4 Figure 3's three-by-two scatter panels into v5 Figure 4's two-by-three display. Other figures are resized or relocated, and four training-loss panels become test-accuracy panels.

improvement.justification: The mathematical corrections, clearer qualifications of the bounds, and code-access information improve clarity and verifiability relative to v4. These gains outweigh limited drawbacks: removing training-loss plots weakens direct checks of near interpolation, and new Appendix A Equation (23) states equality where its argument supports only an upper bound.
